note: How `skynet setup --robot <model>` turns a model name into a driver library. Kinds: prebuilt (builds with make alone; the wizard uses it built, or says how to build it), sdk (links a vendor SDK named in sdk; used built, or refused with the variable), cargo (a Rust driver in the workspace; found in the checkout's target/release, or refused with the cargo command for crate), sim (simulation-only; refused with the reason), python (runs under drivers/python-host; refused with the pointer), host (python-host itself: not a robot), library (shared code other drivers link: not a robot), unmapped (no install mapping yet; refused with the README). Shipped in release bundles so the refusals work without a checkout. lib is always the Linux name: a library built on Windows or macOS will not run on the robot.

fairino.sdk: FAIRINO_SDK (FAIR INNOVATION's client, Apache-2.0, not vendored)

lite3.sdk: LITE3_SDK (Deep Robotics' headers and client, MIT, not vendored)

x1.sdk: X1_INFER (the vendor's built tree) and ROS_ROOT (a ROS 2 install)

apollo.note: an Apptronik Apollo in MuJoCo; guest ceiling, no hardware claim

mujoco.note: a scene file as a body; bench only

lerobot.note: the LeRobot bridge; runs under drivers/python-host

pudu.note: the cloud API over urllib; runs under drivers/python-host

python-host.note: the generic out-of-process Python host; configure the payload per its README

canopen.note: a CiA 402 body over SocketCAN; runs under drivers/python-host

cia402-rs.note: the CiA 402 state machine canopen-rs and ethercat-rs share

ethercat.note: CiA 402 drives over EtherCAT; runs under drivers/python-host

fourier.note: a Fourier GR-1 over RoCS; runs under drivers/python-host

franka.note: a Franka arm over the FCI; runs under drivers/python-host (franka-rs is the host-tier port)

spot.note: Boston Dynamics Spot over bosdyn-client, command-level; runs under drivers/python-host

ur_rtde.note: a UR arm over RTDE; runs under drivers/python-host
